metrics.name: pause_length
metrics.threshold: >= 0.3 s longer than reference, mid-phrase (no punctuation)

regions.explanation: At 17.87s, between “have” and “bestowed,”, a 940 ms silence replaced the reference's 0 ms pause. A long silence where the reference has none - especially mid-phrase - breaks the syntactic unit and signals lost place rather than deliberate emphasis. Fix: Keep this phrase in one breath; pause at the punctuation instead.

regions.text: the generosity and cooperation he has
regions.explanation: From 35.90s to 37.84s (“the generosity and cooperation he has”), loudness relative to the speaker's own level fell 7.8 dB below the reference, bottoming out 9.9 dB down; that is 1.2× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. The loudness falls away across the phrase, so its final words - often the payoff - drop toward the noise floor of the room. Fix: Support the breath through the end of the phrase; the last words need the same energy as the first.

regions.text: have now taken the presidential oath. The words have been
regions.explanation: From 44.80s to 53.08s (“have now taken the presidential oath. The words have been”), articulation rate slowed to 3.09 syll/s against 4.49 syll/s in the reference (-31%); that is 1.2× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. Stretched words without matching emphasis read as hesitation and dilute the rhythm of the phrase; the audience's attention drifts between content words. Fix: Tighten these words to the reference pace; keep length only on the stressed word.
